en: What's all this? My whole body hurts!
Has some fool been beating this old woman?
Hm? Who are you?
Aha, an errand boy from the liquor shop?
I paid off my tab the other day, didn't I?
I am not from the liquor shop.
Hah! So you're saying you greeted me
for no reason at all? You're an odd one.
Oh, never mind. Too much bother to ask.
I'm a busy woman, so I'll be off now.
What? You want something with me?
Well, I wondered what dimwit it was. It's you.
Don't go strutting about like that.
Some of us struggle just to get by each day.
This world sure is unfair.
, hold on a minute.
note: After the name at line start: 'Chris, hold on a minute.'

en: Good timing. Morning to you.
If only a fellow with deep pockets like you
would move into my lodging house.
No meals, mind, but I'd spare you a drink.
Pardon the intrusion.
What do you want? ...Hic.
If you know it's rude, don't ask. Hic.
Have you seen anyone suspicious around here?
...Not that you'd know, I suppose.
Hmph! Stop me, then insult me? How rude!
Be kinder to your elders. Hic.
Don't you make a fool of me... Hic.
...Pardon me.
Well! What an attitude! Hic.
Ask me whatever you like, I won't answer.
Hic... Urp.
You've got time to kill, roaming all over town.
Dunno what you do for a living, mind.
Well, good luck to you.
Oh, it's you. You keeping well?
Even I give a decent greeting
now and then, you know.
I'm glad to see you in good health.
You're an odd man, you are.
Nothing I say ever gets you down.
You must be somebody important, eh?
Ow! Watch where you're going!
Bumping into an old woman. Apologize!
Ah, my apologies.
Are you hurt, old woman?
Who're you calling old? Call me Madeline.
Honestly, I nearly dropped the liquor
I just bought!
Pardon me, then.
Though you seem to be drunk already...
note: No speaker tag; the player's (stern) line, parallel to gentle #10421.

en: What? What's wrong with drinking what I earn?
Quit your nagging.
...Oh, it's you.
What's wrong with drinking in the daytime?
Is there a law says "No drinking by day"?
Oh my. You're fond of a drink too, I see.
I'm much the same.
Old as I am, I drink every day.
Some fools preach, "It's poison for you,"
but at my age, what good is saving
money? I'll drink and enjoy myself.
That work of yours sounds hard.
I hear you've been asking around.
Now, wringing rent out of lodgers like I do,
that's a good job. Easy work.
Oh, we meet again.
Seems you only drink wine,
note: Wine: the vampire's usual cover drink.

en: but I know some fine liquor. Shall I tell you?
Ahh, I'm worn out.
At times like this, a drink's the thing.
Who are you? Looking for lodgings?
No rooms free right now.
What?
Don't tell me you're from the liquor shop?
I paid my tab already. Off with you.
You just don't get it, do you.
I've got no business with you.
You look like you've got money.
How nice it'd be if you were my lodger.
